input.reasoning:
Total backlog = 210 story points across 24 tasks. With only one placeholder role "Team member" at 1 FTE (75 USD/hr, ~40 hrs/week, ~1,800-1,900 productive hours/year), a single person cannot realistically deliver this backlog in a normal project timeframe. I converted story points to engineering hours using a standard heuristic of 1 point ≈ 6 hours of effort (a common mid-range mapping for teams doing mixed frontend/backend/API/data work), giving a raw effort estimate, then priced it entirely against the single "Team member" rate since that is the only role on the rate card.

Raw effort: 210 points x 6 hrs/point = 1,260 hours of pure delivery work.
Added overhead for project management/coordination, QA and rework buffer since there is only one generic role covering everything (no dedicated PM/QA/BA roles exist on the rate card): +20% = 252 hours, and a risk/contingency buffer of +15% given no historical actuals exist to validate the estimate = 189 hours.
Total estimated hours ≈ 1,260 + 252 + 189 = 1,701 hours, all billed to "Team member" at 75 USD/hr = $127,575.

Since the rate card only has one role and one FTE, all hours are allocated to that single line — this is a major capacity constraint (1 FTE can only deliver ~1,800-2,000 hours/year, meaning this backlog alone would consume nearly a full year of that person's capacity, with zero slack for anything else).

Non-labour costs are estimated based on typical needs for a project of this shape (CI/staging infra, Stripe fees setup, Oracle migration tooling, monitoring/observability tooling), since no non-labour costs were specified — these are indicative placeholders only.

Priority breakdown allocates the 1,701 hours proportionally to each task's story points within its priority band (points/210 * total hours * 75 rate), giving a $ total per priority tier.

Scenarios (P50/P80/P95) reflect increasing uncertainty due to the placeholder rate card, no actuals, unclear seniority/skill mix, and a single-person capacity constraint that likely means the real delivery team will need more than 1 FTE — actual final cost is highly likely to exceed this placeholder estimate once real roles/rates are set.

scenarios.name: P50 - Base case (indicative, single placeholder role)
P80 - Likely case with rework/integration risk
P95 - Worst case incl. migration/payment integration risk and true team build-out

nonLabourLines.description: CI/CD and staging environment hosting (cloud infra, pipelines) - est. 6 months setup+run
Stripe integration fees/sandbox testing and reconciliation tooling
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/licensing and one-off extraction costs
Observability/tracing tooling (APM, dashboards, alerting) - annual subscription portion
Accessibility audit/testing tooling and external WCAG 2.2 AA compliance review
Contingency for legacy portal decommission (infra shutdown, redirects, archival storage)

assumptions: Rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: all team members are currently listed generically as 'Team member' at 75 USD/hour with 1 FTE available. No real roles (e.g. developer, QA, PM, BA) or differentiated rates have been assigned yet. This estimate is therefore indicative only and must be revisited once actual roles and rates are configured.
No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet, so this estimate is based purely on backlog sizing heuristics, not empirical velocity or cost data.

Story points converted to effort using a heuristic of 6 hours per point, a mid-range assumption for mixed frontend/backend/integration/data work; actual conversion will vary significantly by real team skill and composition.

A 20% overhead was added for coordination, QA and rework given there is no dedicated PM/QA role in the rate card, and a further 15% contingency was added given the total absence of historical actuals and rate-card uncertainty.

With only 1 FTE staffed under the single 'Team member' role, the allocated ~1,701 hours represents most of a year's full-time capacity for one person — this role is staffed far too thinly to deliver this 210-point backlog in a normal project timeframe; a real team will need multiple people/roles.

Non-labour costs (infrastructure, Stripe integration, Oracle migration tooling, observability, accessibility audit) are rough indicative placeholders based on typical needs for a project of this scope, since no non-labour costs were supplied in the brief.
Priority-band totals are allocated proportionally to each task's story points as a share of total backlog points, multiplied by the total labour cost.
Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) and payment integration (PW-7, 13 points, Urgent) carry the highest technical risk and are the main drivers of the P95 contingency scenario.

Scenario growth (P50 -> P80 -> P95) reflects escalating risk from integration complexity, migration surprises, and the strong likelihood that a single generic FTE role will need to be expanded into a real multi-person team with higher blended rates.
